original_question: Let T be a finite collection of vectors in R^n. Define b(T) = E_{x ~ {-1,1}^n}[max_{t in T} <t,x>] and define g(T) analogously with x replaced by a standard Gaussian vector. Does there always exist a finite collection T' such that g(T') <= O(b(T)) and for every t in T there exists t' in T' with ||t - t'||_1 <= O(b(T))?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the unnumbered open-problem entry titled "Bernoulli Conjecture" in the paper, specifically its statement on page P3, sourced there to Talagrand [Tal94].
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly takes T to be a finite collection of vectors in R^n, defines b(T) as the Bernoulli/Rademacher supremum expectation, defines g(T) as the Gaussian analogue, and asks for a finite collection T' giving both a Gaussian bound g(T') <= O(b(T)) and an l1-approximation condition for every t in T.
missing_details: Make explicit that the conjecture is quantified uniformly over every positive integer n and every finite T subset of R^n.
Specify that T' is also a finite subset of the same ambient space R^n.
For b(T), state that the random vector has independent coordinates uniformly distributed in {-1,1}.
For g(T), state that the random vector is a standard Gaussian in R^n, i.e. has independent N(0,1) coordinates.
For stand-alone readability, define <.,.> as the standard Euclidean inner product.
For stand-alone readability, define ||.||_1 as the l1 norm on R^n.
Clarify that the constants hidden in the two O(b(T)) terms are absolute/universal, independent of n and T.
If you want the question to be maximally paper-faithful, identify it by its title "Bernoulli Conjecture" and note that the paper attributes it to Talagrand [Tal94].
refined_question: Bernoulli Conjecture. Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that for every integer n >= 1 and every finite set T subset of R^n, if one defines b(T) = E[max_{t in T} <t, epsilon>] for epsilon with independent uniform coordinates in {-1,1}, and g(T) = E[max_{t in T} <t, G>] for G with independent N(0,1) coordinates, then there exists a finite set T' subset of R^n such that g(T') <= C b(T) and, for every t in T, there exists t' in T' with ||t - t'||_1 <= C b(T)?
justification: The paper does not contain a numbered Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 relevant to this draft; instead, it lists unnumbered open problems. Your draft matches almost exactly the statement under the heading "Bernoulli Conjecture". The only substantive refinements needed to make it fully stand-alone are to spell out the quantifiers, the ambient space for T', the distributions in b(T) and g(T), the norm/inner-product conventions, and the fact that the hidden constants are universal. The nearby context adds only remarks that g(T) is geometrically understood via Talagrand's majorizing measures theorem and that the source is Talagrand [Tal94]; it does not supply an explicit equivalent reformulation, so no alternate formulation should be added.
